posts.name: Melkhor
posts.cooked:
Yeah, it's the most reliable way of beating Heroic Infinitor if you don't have any handy tricks to make him do damage outside of his own turn. Once all his manifestations are out, the game *should* end on Infinitor's next turn, provided you've made sure he has enough HP left to survive his madness loop longer than his remaining manifestations.

Honestly, I've never even seen Heroic Infinitor flip, and unless you're playing to deliberately flip him as soon as possible (for some arcane reason), I doubt most teams could even hope to survive that situation.

posts.name: jstnmayo
posts.cooked: I had a game of regular heroic infinitor where he did flip and i thought i was going to lose. I had a 3-H team of Dark visionary, DW Nightmist, and a 3rd hero who i don't remeber who got incaped almost imeadaitly. I was playing in final wasteland and had con's bunker, the library, and unforgiving out. I had already gotten a bend the ether on infintior so when he fliped i just cocooned and Nightmist had her eldar god amulet. i organized the damage from infintor to not kill the enviroments but that the 2 damage that they deal themselves would removing them all from the game and between all the extra card draw from the enviroment, double skipping, and the incaped hero nightmist was able to redirect enough damage to stay alive. It ended with visonary having her entire deck in hand, having 2 bend the ethers on infinitor and just playing mind spike while nightmist redirected damage back to infinitor.
